notes.title: Operator #10 Enters the Zerzura: Field Surgeon "Hela" Joins Zero Division!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

It’s been over half a year since Zero Division launched, and we’re incredibly grateful for the unwavering support from our community. Many of you continue to share your passion and suggestions across platforms, and to everyone around the globe—thank you!

We've been telling you folks that the game will keep improving from the launch. And yes, Zero Division is still evolving, with the major update we present to you today!

One of the game's biggest highlights has always been its diverse, mechanically-unique Operators, and we've been working hard to expand that roster with fresh roles and gameplay mechanics. In the cyberpunk world of Zero Division, a battle-hardened medic who’s both precise and deadly is a rare but vital asset. 
[h3]Today, we’re excited to introduce our newest Operator on the roster: [b]Hela, the Field Surgeon[/b].[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/f9bd7c59928da179daea4f96ed52462ddc69c53d.png[/img]

[i]"Mercenaries rely on the field surgeon corps to treat their injuries and inoculate them against the dangerous biohazards of Zerzura. But when it comes to Hela? She's more interested in finding novel ways to kill than cure.
Her expertise in genomic engineering is second to none, yet she harbors an unsettling obsession with the grotesque. Like a viper slithering through the ruins, Hela joins the crew to validate her research on a novel batch of test subjects... and if there's a few "ethical standards" being violated here and there, who's to complain?"[/i]

[b]Operator Mechanics:[/b]

Hela specializes in debuff-focused combat, applying status effects via cards and summons while instantly triggering them through her attacks. Many of you have shared feedback that negative-status-based playstyles felt underwhelming due to their delayed impact. Now, Hela's arrival shakes up the meta - now is the time to punish your enemies instantly with those debuffs!

[h3][b]New Augments[/b][/h3]
[b]Occult Sign[/b] – At the start of the round, a random ally and a random enemy each gain +3 [b]Attack[/b] and +2 [b]Armor[/b] until the end of the round.
[b]Lion Cadent[/b] – Your [b]Shots[/b] are now affected by [b]Momentum[/b].
[b]Nine of Swords[/b] – If you would gain [b]Block[/b], gain [b]Attack[/b] instead.

That’s all for this update! We’d love for you to jump in and test out these new additions. Your continued support means the world to us, and we’ll keep pushing to make Zero Division even better.

See you in the Exclusion Zone!

notes.title: Patch 1.03
notes.content:
[b]Patch 1.03[/b]
[b]15 August 2024[/b]

[b]Features / Quality of Life Fixes[/b]

- Added a new Gallery, accessible from the main menu (bottom right corner), where players can browse all cards and augments in the game.
- Added a new "Run in Background" gameplay setting in the options menu (default is enabled). If this setting is disabled, the game will pause when it is not the active window, which should significantly reduce CPU/GPU load.
- Added a two-step confirmation prompt when attempting to exit out of a run after winning the game or being defeated.

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]

- Fixed boss names not being properly localised in the end of run report.
- Fixed an issue associated with attempting to switch to another Hub screen immediately after opening a data shard or salvage.

[b]Balance Changes[/b]

- Reduced the cost of various choices in events which require Gleam. 

[i]Notes: Some event choices that cost Gleam were very expensive compared to the costs of buying equivalent goods or services at the Broker. These have been adjusted to make them more attractive.[/i]

[b]Known Issues[/b]

- We are investigating an issue where imprinting a card into the Failsafe doesn't work in certain situations. If you are encountering this issue, please do send a player log (usually located at [user name]\AppData\LocalLow\Robot Cat Limited\Zero Division\Player.log) to our support email address.

notes.title: Patch 1.02
notes.content:
[b]Patch 1.02[/b]
[b]5 August 2024[/b]

[b]Features / Quality of Life Fixes[/b]

- Added a new "Fast Vault Opening" setting in the options menu. Enabling this setting greatly speeds up the Shard and Salvage opening animations, and also the Draft Mode opening animations.
- Added a new "Minimum" graphics quality setting in the options menu. Using this quality level will disable all 3D models in-game to maximise performance. [b]As a result of this change, you may need to readjust the quality settings the first time you enter the game[/b].
- Drag-to-attack should now be more responsive.
- Right-clicking anywhere in the main Hub will now take you to the Expedition map screen.
- Pressing Left Ctrl in Combat will now toggle showing / hiding targets.
- Slightly increased the font size for all cards.

[b]Balance Changes[/b]

- Mayhem's Exhilaration now always heals on Strike damage, no matter Mayhem's current HP. Mayhem's max HP has been adjusted to 25 to compensate.
- Mayhem's Nutcracker and Piledriver cards no longer cause self-damage.
- Mayhem's Fulminate card now draws a card in addition to its other effects.

[i]Notes: Mayhem was previously weaker than the other two Guardians in terms of defensive ability. These changes are intended to make her self-healing toolkit more consistent.[/i]

- Aim now increases Shot damage by 4 (up from 3).

[i]Notes: Whilst Typhon and Aleph were situationally strong, their upper-end potential was generally lower than that of the other, non-Shot focused operators. This tweak is intended to slightly improve their Shot-based pay-offs.[/i]

[b]Known Issues[/b]

- We are investigating an issue where imprinting a card into the Failsafe doesn't work in certain situations.

notes.title: Roadmap Update: The Future of "Zero Division"
notes.content:
[b]July 18, 2024[/b]

Hi everyone!

It has been a week since the release of "Zero Division." During this past week, we have received tremendous amount of support from our community and provided us with a ton of meaningful feedback and suggestions! First and foremost, we want to express our most sincere gratitude – Thank y’all very much!

Due to the limited capacity and resources, we have recently been focusing our efforts on addressing high-priority issues for the game post-launch, including but not limited to usability issues, bug fixes, and some design flaws that were not very user-intuitive. Many of these issues could not have been identified without extensive player feedback from the community, so once again, thank you.

At the same time, we haven't forgotten the community's bigger and louder questions: What does the future hold for "Zero Division"? Will it be left at its current status? Will development stop here? The answer is most certainly “No.” We have been consistent with our answers to those questions from the beginning when responding to players’ reviews on the Store page and comments in the discussion board. Now, with many of you having consumed the content of the game fairly quickly, we believe it is necessary to make an official announcement: both the publishing and development teams are committed to keep updating "Zero Division" to make it better in the foreseeable future.

“Why not sooner?” you may ask, well, the reason we are posting this write-up today is simply that now we finally have a rough plan for the first steps — although it is still “rough” and needs further work, we hope by sharing it with the community, we can communicate with our community to seek additional input. It is you who have validated that the gameplay is interesting, it is you who have been telling us that this card game is not too shabby. Now, we want to commit to our supporters and let them know what are some important tasks on our semi-short term action list for “Zero Division”.

[u][b]Features[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] [b]In-Game Glossary Base: [/b]A self-explanatory feature, which is designed to be a pop-up menu option that can be accessed anywhere regardless if you are in-game or not. 
[*] [b]Card Gallery: [/b]Allows easy-viewing of card illustrations of already-collected cards, as well as their descriptive tooltips.
[*] [b]Augment Library: [/b]Similarly, allow easy-viewing of already-collected augments with full tooltips.
[/list]
[u][b]UX/UI/QoL[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Option to Skip the Unpacking Animation: The current animation sometime gets a bit annoying after you play and become familiar of the game. We obviously don’t want to take away the fun in opening packs, so an animation toggle is something we believe could be reasonable.
[*] Option to Disable 3D Animation: To provide a smoother game experience on PC with lower specs.
[*] Two-Step Confirmation for Quitting the Game: To prevent players from accidentally quitting from a perfect combat/run!
[*] Improved UX/UI Design: The current UX/UI design logic for players to go back to the main expedition screen a bit cumbersome, so we are looking at a possible, improved solution.
[/list]

We are fully aware that there are still many areas in the current version of the game that requires further improvements and tweaks. We’ve been addressing them since day 1 and we will not be turning away from those issues. Alongside with the regular bug fixes, we’ll be planning and working on those tasks accordingly. Of course, please rest assured that in the long-run, we plan to add more cards, more operators, more augments, more levels, more challenging enemies and bosses with interesting mechanics to “Zero Division” (and some of this work has already started)!

This is the current support plan and road map of "Zero Division." It is our community that has given "Zero Division" a clearer direction for the road ahead, and we will follow that. We would greatly appreciate your continued support in the future!

Sincerely,

“Zero Division” Developer: Robot Cat Games
“Zero Division” Publisher: Astrolabe Games

*On a side note, our poor dev got hit with the COVID variant, so the patching will be slowing down a bit... But please rest assured that Zero Division will see continued support as committed!

notes.title: Hotfix 1.01k
notes.content:
[b]Hotfix 1.01k[/b]
[b]16 July 2024[/b]

[b]Balance Changes[/b]

- The Camouflage ability in the Silichameleon and Starstalker encounters has been reworked. Now, enemies with the new ability (Chameleon) only become untargetable after they drop below 50% HP.

[i]Notes: The old version of Camouflage has very little possibility of interaction for operators focused on card-based strategies. This iteration opens up counterplay, whilst retaining some of the original design intent.[/i]

[b]New Cards Available[/b]

- Certain rare cards can be unlocked from challenges and by completing difficulty levels. Previously, these cards were not being properly unlocked. This has now been fixed, and these cards have been added to the card pool. (This is automatic, and players do not need to replay any difficulty or redo any challenge.)

- These cards will appear either in Sidereal Shards (for AGI-Forged cards), or as rare drops in Aphotic Shards (for non-AGI-forged cards). Once unlocked, they will also appear in Draft Mode. Use these new tools and allies to annihilate your enemies!

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]

- We identified the source of the issue where playing Renegade's Recklessness would result in a reduction in Renegade's attack. This only occurs if Renegade has Goliath Servo Suit installed, because the negative effect on armor reduces the bonus attack granted by the augment. We have made a small tweak so that Goliath Servo Suit cannot grant negative attack (i.e., if Renegade's armor is negative).
- Fixed some incorrect localised text in the Phase counter.

notes.title: Hotfix 1.01e
notes.content:
[b]Hotfix 1.01e[/b]
[b]13 July 2024[/b]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]

- Although the last hotfix did resolve the Malevolence targeting issue for some players, we are aware that a number of players are still finding it difficult to target the boss properly. Although we can't fully reproduce the bug at this stage, we believe we have identified a potential cause of the problem and this hotfix includes an experimental fix to this issue. Third time lucky!

- Fixed the challenges which require completing a run with 3 operators of the same class.
- Fixed an issue with Paladin's Energize card when played on a non-operator ally.
- Fixed an intermittent bug which occasionally caused additional copies of the starting neutral cards to be added to operators' decks when starting a new campaign.
- Fixed a decimal point error with displaying the Win Rate % in the Challenges screen.
- Fixed a possible issue with the Satellite Rain challenge not triggering properly in some circumstances.

[b]Balance Changes[/b]

- Mayhem's HP has been increased to 30 (up from 20) and her attack has been increased to 3 (up from 2).

[i]Notes: Mayhem's low HP meant that she was too fragile in comparison to the other Guardian operators. Mayhem is intended to be a more offensive Guardian who tanks by dealing Strike damage, with a corresponding weakness that her HP is subject to much sharper swings. This buff is intended to preserve these characteristics, whilst making her more viable for higher difficulty play. We will continue to monitor and tweak Mayhem's toolkit as required.[/i]

- The Nightweavers encounter in Blindside Ruins has been adjusted slightly to make it less lethal.

[i]Notes: Although some encounters are intended to counter specific operator builds, these mechanics are normally restricted to elite and boss fights. The Nightmare version of this normal encounter was a little too punitive, especially since this appears in Act 1. Accordingly, the HP and damage values have been adjusted to make this encounter slightly easier.[/i]

notes.title: Zero Division Officially Launches TODAY!
notes.content:
Hello, operators.

Welcome to Zerzura! 

Zero Division officially launches today. We’d like to thank you for your continued support and feedback!

Taking this opportunity, here is a detailed rundown of the scope of the game, as well as key features and content available in Zero Division on the first day to help you get on track and better prepare you for the complex game mechanics and extensive content! 

[i]*We will continue to support the game after launch via timely updates, aiming to improve balance and make gameplay adjustments based on community feedback. Of course, we also plan to add more content in the future to further increase the scope of the game. Please rest assured that we will keep improving the game. Details will be shared with you later.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/661dec0c6b7b50c8bbb69a837c101d98b0b2dd99.jpg[/img]

[h2][u]Standard Campaign Mode[/u][/h2]

This mode is essentially the staple roguelite deckbuillder game experience – go on an expedition, craft your own deck, and eliminate whoever (or whatever) stands in your way with your powerful build! Simply put, choose three operators to form your squad, explore different levels, encounter various events (good or bad!), and face all kinds of evil minions and fearsome bosses! 

Upon completing the expedition, earn rewards and unlock higher difficulties. However, be aware that your actions in your expedition will consume action points called "[b]Supplies[/b]." Each level starts with 7 supplies by default. Once consumed, you can continue exploring, but you won't receive the corresponding rewards.

We are confident you will gradually master the game by learning about the unique design of Zero Division and discovering the fun of deck building as you overcome seemingly impossible challenges. As you progress through the difficulties, you will climb higher on the corporate ladder and unlock other gameplay modes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/7781a0c8522b5984f54bc4041a728a579afb4b17.jpg[/img]

[h2][u]The Combat[/u][/h2]

The combat in Zero Division features classic turn-based card gameplay, requiring you to manage multiple tasks: spending character action points (AP) to play or deploy cards for that turn, dragging and dropping character cards to perform basic attacks (which don't consume AP), and activating character skills by clicking their icons in the lower left corner of their corresponding character card.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/5ad6ab93e8d9c91b0ca10a03910af571375e86b3.jpg[/img]

[h2][u]11+ Difficulty Tiers[/u][/h2]

Like many deck-building games, Zero Division has a wealth of stories and content initially locked. Players will progress through the 11 difficulty tiers by completing challenging expeditions, climbing the corporate ladder for better rewards, more operators, more gameplay modes, and hidden secrets! For those elite operators who can conquer everything, completing all difficulty tiers unlocks a custom difficulty setting for ultimate challenges.

[h2][u]Assemble Your Crew[/u][/h2]

Assemble your crew of 3 from 9 steadfast operators, split into 3 core archetypes: Guardian, Assault, and Specialist, mimicking the classic tank-healer-dps dealer triangle in classic MMO games.

[h3]Guardians: Solid damage absorbers.[/h3]
[list]
[*] Paladin: A veteran soldier whose Block doesn't expire at the start of each round.
[*] Jinn: A mercenary captain who deals damage to attackers every time he is hit.
[*] Mayhem: A techno anarchist who restores HP with her signature combat ability.
[/list]

[h3]Assaults: Known for high damage output.[/h3]
[list]
[*] Renegade: A rogue troubleshooter who has ability to “Rally” herself when needed at a cost (to attack multiple times in one round).
[*] Rook: A corporate headhunter who will gain 1 action point for each Strike card she plays.
[*] Typhon: A cold cyborg killer with special bonuses for both Strike and Shot cards.
[/list]

[h3]Specialists: Excel at strategic & tactic combat.[/h3]
[list]
[*] Mirage: A holo prodigy who can actively create hard-light clones of herself at will.
[*] Tinker: A master engineer who can rig up powerful fusion grenades.
[*] Aleph: An augmented sniper whose Shots always hit the mark with her unfaltering Aim.
[/list]

Choose to field a classic party with one of each archetype, or mix things up with unconventional compositions. Any combination is viable, provided you have the skill to guide them through the trials of Zerzura City. There is no true protagonist in this game: with the right cards and augmentations, any operator can have their turn to shine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/7e724a24c6e31877e2aadf6257904b3a2a1e87f9.jpg[/img]

[h2][u]Game Scope[/u][/h2]

There are a total of 6 different locations for you to explore in Zero Division. Each expedition involves choosing and thoroughly investigating 3 of these locations. You will need to deal with various killer robots, mutants, and cyborgs, with difficult bosses appearing randomly at the end of each level. There are hundreds of cards and dozens of augmentations for you to explore and discover.

However, the full content won’t be available in your first playthrough. Try completing the lowest difficulty first and progress from there!

[h2][u]Meta-progression[/u][/h2]

Earn [b]Mnemosynth[/b] (a special currency) through your runs, and use these synthetic memories to permanently imprint cards into your collection through the Failsafe system. The added cards can be carried over to the future runs to get you a step closer to your favourite build next time when you set off. Additionally, you can also use Mnemosynth to further enhance your favourite operators’ skills and special abilities – they make quite a difference in play!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/cf1d0399cbb23e10468c9de8cd08caed84fba2fa.jpg[/img]

Whew, so this concludes our introduction, quite a bit, isn’t it? We will be actively listening and collecting feedback and comments from the community in order to bring you the best deckbuilding gameplay experience as well as more exciting content.

Hope you enjoy Zero Division!

Thanks!

The Developer & The Publishing Team of Zero Division

notes.title: Cyberpunk-themed DBG “Zero Division” Launches July 12 on Steam!
notes.content:
Hi Everyone,

Today we'd like to proudly announce that the cyberpunk-themed CCG roguelite deckbuilder, “Zero Division,” will be officially released on July 12, 2024, on Steam, 12.99USD with 10% launch discount.

Easy to pick up but hard to master, with a deep, tactical core and a wealth of encounter mechanisms inspired by classic MMOs, Zero Division is here to provide card game fans with the ultimate experience. The game features nine unique operators, each with its own deck, three distinct gameplay modes, eleven progressively unlocked difficulty tiers, six different stages filled with random events and formidable enemies, and hundreds of meticulously designed cards.


[h3]Assemble Your Crew[/h3]
Assemble your crew of 3 from 9 steadfast operators, split into 3 core archetypes: Guardian, Assault, and Specialist. Choose to field a classic party with one of each archetype, or mix things up with unconventional compositions. Any combination is viable, provided you have the skill to guide them through the trials of Zerzura City. There is no true protagonist in this game: with the right cards and augmentations, any operator can have their turn to shine.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/9cd61f8ba936169c8d54c42defe62c93b3874732.png[/img]

[h3]Fight With CCG-Style Decks[/h3]
Each operator comes with their own deck containing at least 8 signature cards and at least 12 free slots. These resistance fighters are all armed to the teeth: each customisable deck must contain at least 20 cards; and any exposed weaknesses means certain death. To succeed, exploit the synergies between your decks and devise inspired new tactics to defeat your foes.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/bd226e7dcb32ef8573bf2e63ce56b0654909ce4f.png[/img]

[h3]MMO-Inspired Bosses[/h3]
Engage in combat against multi-phase boss encounters inspired by MMO raid bosses, each with their own exhilarating mechanics and unique abilities. Take on the Siegebreaker, a colossal mech war machine; spill the blood of the Abomination, a terrible experiment gone awry; or defend a rooftop against a gunship blazing with weapons.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/a00e8572f0b1201dff0eaaaac06a0bb1a15d9e63.png[/img]

[h3]Campaign Mode[/h3]
Make your way through 3 out of 6+ shattered districts before reaching the culmination of your journey in Wargentin District, the dark heart of the Zerzura Exclusion Zone. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/1e6c9e06325aaae5c9912e51f0cd12bea835b4b2.png[/img]

[h3]Draft Mode[/h3]
Inspired by drafting formats in CCGs, draft mode starts you off with a veritable arsenal of data shards. Unseal your shards, draft the cards within to create your decks, and then take those decks into battle against an unforgiving gauntlet of randomized, escalating boss encounters. How far can you get before you succumb to the most dangerous enemies in Zerzura?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/f01667510287e2f662d764210b5434bb531efb05.png[/img]

[h3]Meta-progression[/h3]
Earn Mnemosynth through your runs, and use these synthetic memories to permanently imprint cards into your collection through the Failsafe system. The added cards can be carried over to the next run, greatly enhancing your deck’s power.

Don´t forget to add Zero Division to your wishlist.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2181950/Zero_Division/

notes.title: The Big Demo Update
notes.content:
Hello, operators!

We're excited to be part of WePlay Expo 2023 & Turn-Based Carnival 2023, and we've been hard at work on a new demo - bringing together new features and a host of changes in response to player feedback. So, without further ado, onto the new content!

[b]Gameplay[/b]
[list]
[*] All operators' cards are now shown on-screen in combat. There's no need to switch between operators' decks!
[*] Operators now start the game with 3 cards, and draw up to 3 cards each turn.
[/list]
[b]New Operator - Mayhem[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/889f838003a3de957c8a05f887d09c3bf41d8f20.png[/img][list]
[*] Mayhem, an anarchic [b]Guardian[/b] operator, has been added to the demo.
[*] Mayhem has one of the lowest HP pools in the game, but makes up for it with her powerful [b]Exhilaration[/b] passive ability, enabling her to heal HP from Strikes whenever she's below 50% HP.
[*] Take Mayhem's HP below the threshold and keep the heat off your allies by making use of her unique [b]Fulminate[/b] card, which forces enemies to attack her immediately.
[*] Then, use her powerful [b]Nutcracker[/b] or [b]Tornado Swing[/b] cards to heal herself back up whilst dealing damage to her enemies!
[/list]
[b]New Operator - Aleph[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/ba2ec14aa0fdeb60e8ef5387580311c2f1d6f6d3.png[/img][list]
[*] Aleph, a sniper [b]Specialist[/b] operator, has been added to the demo.
[*] Thanks to her [b]Unerring Aim[/b] passive ability, Aleph's Aim stacks never expire - so zero-in on targets by building Aim stacks with her [b]Eliminator Rifle[/b].
[*] Once her Aim is true, destroy your enemies or heal your allies with her flexible [b]Adaptive Shot[/b].
[*] Double up on Aim stacks by switching to [b]Sniper Stance[/b], or shoot again by retrieving your expended Shots using Aleph's [b]Eidetic Memory[/b].
[/list]
[b]New Feature - Talents[/b]
[list]
[*] All operators now have a [b]talent tree[/b], accessible through the Crew Panel in the Hub.
[*] Talents can change your operators' signature cards and sometimes their roles - switch Typhon into a powerful defender, or build Renegade into a fire-spewing nightmare!
[*] Unlocking an operator's capstone talent row also provides that operator with a powerful second ability.
[/list]
[b]New Feature - Enemy & Event Revamp + Difficulties[/b]
[list]
[*] All the enemy encounters and events have been revamped to provide for more varied and interesting encounters.
[*] In addition, difficulty modes have been added for those wanting more of a challenge.
[/list]
[b]New Feature - Modes[/b]
[list]
[*] A new Exploration mode has been added to the game, which provides for unlimited Supply and relaxed deckbuilding limits!
[*] Draft mode has been folded into the Campaign as a new mode.
[/list]
[b]New Feature - Save Game[/b]
[list]
[*] Games are now automatically saved, and can be continued by using the Continue button in the Main Menu.
[/list]
[b]Known Issues[/b]
[list]
[*] JP localisation is still in progress and isn't available in this version.
[/list]
We hope you enjoy these updates, and we'd very much appreciate any feedback - either complete the in-game survey from the Main Menu, or leave a comment here on the Steam forums!

- Robot Cat

notes.title: Patch 0.62 - Zero Division Demo Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43076299/cb4b4d210037560ea9af238d53613e60db4db472.png[/img]

Hello, operators!

We've just released [b]Patch 0.62[/b], which includes a few bug fixes and a number of UI/UX improvements in response to feedback received from players. Here are the patch notes in full!

- Robot Cat

[b]Patch Notes - 0.62[/b]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed a critical bug where playing Mockingjack would cause the game to freeze.
[/list]
[b]UI/UX[/b]
[list]
[*] Added a Settings button to the main menu.

[i]The settings button in the top right hand corner of the UI was too small and easily missed. A more prominent Settings button has now been added to the central button grouping in the main menu.[/i]

[*] Added a help overlay for the campaign hub.

[i]The hub panel UI can be confusing for first-time players. A contextual help overlay is available in the top right hand corner of the UI, but it was small and easily missed. Now, the help overlay for each panel displays automatically the first time a player enters the relevant panel (but not on subsequent playthroughs).[/i]

[*] Dialogue and warning tooltips now persist for longer.

[i]The combat dialogue and hub warning prompts disappeared too quickly to be read in full. These now persist on-screen for a longer period of time.[/i]

[*] Card and mod keyword tooltips are now displayed next to the card or mod.

[i]The keyword tooltips displayed on the left hand side of the combat UI were easily missed due to the focus being on the player's hand and the central board. To make these more prominent, keyword tooltips are now displayed next to the hovered card or mod.[/i]

[*] Playing a card that targets any unit will now cause enemies to display their attack targets.

[i]Having to hover over individual units when deciding which unit a card should target was a nuisance. Now, all enemy attack targets are automatically shown during targeting for easier decision-making.[/i]

[*] Pressing Tab during the main phase now switches between operators' decks, and pressing Escape during targeting now cancels the card play.

[i]Players suggested that having more keyboard shortcuts would be helpful to streamline the gameplay.[/i]

[*] Added a phase counter to the new round text.

[i]It was previously unclear how many phases needed to be cleared in a boss encounter. The new round splash text now displays how many phases the current combat encounter has, and which phase the player is currently on.[/i]

[*] Changed the wording of the Rally tooltip and the rules text for cards that require an ally to be sacrificed.

[i]It was somewhat confusing that cards that have a Rally effect (e.g. Galvanize) couldn't target active units. The tooltip has been changed to make it clear that Rally effects can only target Exhausted units. Similarly, cards that require the elimination of an ally unit  (e.g. Splinter Shard, which requires a Mirage Clone to be sacrificed) can't be played without an ally being deployed. The text has been updated to make this clearer.[/i]
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.591 - Zero Division Open Alpha
notes.content:
Hello, operators!

The Zero Division Open Alpha has been running for a few days now, and the feedback we've received from our playtesters has been fantastic in helping us steer our efforts in improving players' experience. We've read and considered every word, and we're pleased to present the first batch of changes in this [b]Patch 0.591[/b].

Below, you'll find a list of some of the most common issues, and how Patch 0.591 aims to address them. Additional changes - which require more work and which we haven't yet had time to implement - will follow in later patches, including changes to the Failsafe system and additional UI refinements.

[b]Patch Notes - 0.591[/b]

[b]Key Changes[/b]
[list]
[*] [i]Feedback: The text size is too small / I can't see what's happening / This game is made for ants[/i]

Most of the UI text and card text have been increased in size. Tooltips on mods and augments have been reworked to be larger.

[*][i]Feedback: The attack animation takes too long / Playing cards takes too long[/i]

We've made some refinements to make playing cards faster. In addition, a slider has been added on top of the "End Round" button which allows players to skip the attack animation, allowing for much faster attacks. This setting is on by default. Please note that this is experimental, and may result in a few bugs.

[*][i]Feedback: The dialogue moves too fast / The dialogue can't be skipped[/i]

All of the dialogue now persists for longer to give players an opportunity to read the text. All individual pieces of dialogue, including in the tutorial, can now be skipped by pressing spacebar. In addition, an entire conversation can be skipped by clicking the cross on the top right corner of the dialogue box.

[*][i]Feedback: Please add an easier way to switch between operators' hands (other than clicking the portraits in the bottom left corner)[/i]

You can now switch between operators' hands by right-clicking the operator's unit on the game board.
[/list]
[b]UI/UX[/b]
[list]
[*] Cards and mods which refer to card types (Tactic, Gear, Shot, and Strike) will now display the icon of the relevant type next to the text. This was previously inconsistently displayed only in certain cards and mods.
[*] Cooldown icons have been added to activated abilities for improved readability.
[*] The "live" area in the Vault where data shards could be dragged was smaller than intended. This has been fixed.
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] A critical bug causing soft-locks when playing the Oilpetal Venom card has been fixed.
[*] Brainstorm was working incorrectly, and could be played even if the owner was Exhausted. The effect has been changed to target an unexhausted ally (which may be the card owner), and now draws 2 cards instead of 3.
[/list]
A huge thanks to the playtesters for providing your feedback. It's much appreciated, and we hope you will continue to help us improve!

- Robot Cat
